hints: A balanced sequence tree can split at a position and join sequences.
Cut the requested substring by splitting before and after it.
Join the remaining prefix and suffix, then append the cut part.
analogy: Cut a ribbon into three pieces and move the middle piece to the end.
example: Cut positions 2 through 3 from ABCDE: the pieces A, BC, DE become ADEBC.
algorithm: Store characters in an implicit treap, a randomized balanced tree ordered by sequence position, with subtree sizes. Split before a and after b to get prefix, middle and suffix; merge prefix with suffix and then middle. Traverse the final tree in order.
correctness: The splits isolate exactly the requested positions in their original order. The merges concatenate the three pieces in precisely the order specified by the operation, preserving all characters.
complexity: For string length n and m operations, expected O(n+m log n) time and O(n) space with linear-time treap construction.
